reasoning:
I'm noticing a possible gap between the two reports: round 1 checked several geometric orderings but apparently never tested increasing-x order specifically, while round 2 found that increasing x matches nearly all multi-cube episodes. This isn't necessarily a contradiction — round 1's "not any geometric sort" conclusion may have simply missed testing x-order directly.

Given the single exception episode, I'm weighing whether to annotate using the true pick order (keeping fidelity but creating unpredictability) versus annotating with increasing-x universally (creating consistency but introducing a wrong label in that one episode). I'm leaning toward keeping the true pick order as the annotation and instead having the policy's written list follow increasing-x at the button-press step, so the two align in all but one episode, with the mismatch confined to that single case.

I'll keep the annotator prompt mostly as-is but note that it typically coincides with increasing-x order, and update the policy's memory phrasing from "listed order" to increasing-x, plus revise the subgoal rule for the button-press step to target the smallest-x highlighted cube with a tolerance clause. Since round 1 never tested x-ordering specifically, this counts as new evidence worth committing, so I need to edit the text carefully, quoting the exact passages to change.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step; on the button-press step itself, the first entry of the list just written), using the current position of the cube seen there in the scene (cube positions wobble; use the cube visible nearest the stored point).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step). On the button-press step itself (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) there is no carried-in list: point at the cube sitting on a highlighted area that has the smallest x (the robot's right-most highlighted cube), using its current position. To locate the stored entry in the scene: point at the visible cube that lies within about 15 px of the stored entry if there is one; if no listed cube is within that radius (the gripper hovering above a cube often hides it from the object list), point at the stored entry itself, or at that cube's position in the most recent execution step where it was listed near the stored entry. Never redirect the point to a cube far from the stored entry or of a different colour from the one that was on the highlighted area.

edits.modify_from: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, in the order the areas are listed.
edits.modify_to: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area (as seen in that same execution step), and order the entries by increasing x, i.e. the robot's right-most cube first and the left-most cube last, regardless of the order the areas are printed in. e.g. [[107, 97], [116, 135], [80, 145]].

edits.modify_from: Order the entries in the sequence the episode actually picks those cubes up, as read from the later pick-up steps, so the cube picked up next is always the first entry.
edits.modify_to: Order the entries in the sequence the episode actually picks those cubes up, as read from the later pick-up steps, so the cube picked up next is always the first entry. In nearly every episode that sequence is increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last); when the episode's pick order and increasing-x order agree, the list is simply the cubes sorted by increasing x.

revision.refused: The report asks that the annotation itself be written in increasing-x order even in the one episode whose recorded pick order is a rotation of it. That stays out: the annotated list is what makes rule 3 sufficient at every later step, and writing a knowingly wrong order into it would make the policy fail at every pick step of that episode instead of only at its button-press step. The annotation keeps the true pick order (round 1), with the note that it normally equals increasing x; the policy writes increasing x at the button-press step, which is the only step where it must guess, and follows the carried-in list from the front everywhere else. Round 1's refusal of geometric orderings is not undone: that round tested y, gripper distance, button distance, listed order and reverse order, never x, so the increasing-x key is new evidence rather than a contradicted one.
